title: Write a short script that sounds spoken
summary: Write and compress a public-interest video script whose cadence, turns, and ending work aloud instead of reading like an essay.
originNote: A familiar spoken-script control with a hard duration change and a ban on listicle structure.

setup.instructions: Run every turn in order in one fresh workspace. The model must create and then revise only script.md.

turns.content: Write `script.md` for a 90-second spoken video about why public benches matter. Use only these supplied facts: benches support rest, informal meetings, waiting, people-watching, and access for those who cannot walk long distances; their placement can welcome lingering or quietly discourage it. Begin inside one concrete moment, make one clear turn in the middle, and end on an image rather than a slogan. Write words for a human mouth, not an essay with headings. Do not invent statistics.

Revise `script.md` in place for 60 seconds. Keep the opening moment, middle turn, and final image. Do not solve the cut by turning the script into a numbered list or speeding through compressed prose.

checks.description: script.md is plausibly speakable in 60 seconds and has no headings or numbered-list structure.
